$comment: Single source of truth for every free-tier limit asserted by the shipfree skill.
Every value was read from the upstream documentation and is re-verified by
harness/check_limits.py against the platform's own documentation source.
Do not hand-edit a 'value' field to silence a drift report: update the
upstream reading, then re-run the checker.
'doc_label' scopes a value to one upstream table row so a value that is
removed or renamed is reported as drift rather than passing silently.
'doc_key' selects a secondary document for platforms that split their
limits across more than one page.

requests_per_day.note: Resets at 00:00 UTC. Exceeding it returns Cloudflare error 1027. You can choose fail-open or fail-closed routing.

cpu_time_per_invocation.note: The single most important number on this page, and the reason most AI workloads do not belong in a free Worker. The paid plan allows 5 minutes.

subrequests_per_invocation.note: Subrequests to internal services (KV, D1, R2) have their own, larger budget of 1,000.

simultaneous_outgoing_connections.note: Relevant when proxying to several model APIs at once.

request_body_size.note: Set by the Cloudflare account plan, not by the Workers plan.

response_body_size.note: Response body size is not capped by the Workers plan.

storage_per_account.note: Unlimited on Workers Paid. Storage is measured in GB (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes), not GiB.

number_of_objects.note: Within an account or of a given class.

cpu_per_request.note: This is the escape hatch from the 10 ms Worker limit: every incoming request or WebSocket message resets the CPU budget to 30 seconds, configurable up to 5 minutes of active CPU time.

free_tier_reset.value: Daily free limits reset at 00:00 UTC
free_tier_reset.note: Free-tier Durable Object limits are daily, not monthly.

included_requests_per_month.note: The included allocation on the Workers Paid plan.

included_duration_gb_s_per_month.note: Duration is billed in GB-seconds: seconds multiplied by memory in GB.

price_per_million_requests.note: Charged beyond the included allocation on Workers Paid.

pending_io_holds_memory.note: A pending I/O operation keeps the object resident, and billable, for up to 15 minutes.

doc_labels.max_row_size: Maximum string, BLOB or table row size

queries_per_worker_invocation.note: Workers Paid allows 1,000. This is the D1-specific budget: a free Worker may only issue 50 D1 queries per request, so batch reads into a single call instead of looping.

time_travel_retention.note: Point-in-time recovery window. Workers Paid allows 30 days.

max_row_size.note: Maximum string, BLOB or table row size.

writes_to_different_keys_per_day.note: The asymmetry with reads is the trap: reading a cached value is cheap, persisting state is not. Use KV as a cache, not as a database.

minimum_cache_ttl.note: The smallest value you can pass to cacheTtl.

storage.note: Billed on the average peak storage per day across the billing period. Standard storage only.

class_a_operations.note: List, Put, Copy and similar metadata operations.

egress.note: The reason to prefer R2 over S3 on a free tier: there is no egress charge at all.

infrequent_access_storage.value: does not apply to Infrequent Access storage
infrequent_access_storage.note: The free tier covers Standard storage only.

message_size.note: Around 100 bytes of that is internal metadata.

consumer_cpu_time.note: A queue consumer gets far more CPU time than an ordinary Worker. Run heavy work here rather than in the request path.

free_neurons_per_day.note: Resets at 00:00 UTC. Exceeding it fails further operations.

price_per_1000_neurons.note: On the Workers Paid plan, above the free allocation.

text_generation_requests_per_minute.note: Unless the model requires the Workers Paid plan.

embeddings_requests_per_minute.note: The bge-large-en-v1.5 model is limited to 1500.

paid_only_models.note: These require a Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits, so they are not available on a strictly free account. The list is asserted verbatim so that adding or removing a model is reported as drift.

proxied_request_timeout.note: Applies to every plan. A long-lived WebSocket connection follows a different path from a proxied request.

platform_matrix.best_for: Streaming AI APIs and realtime agents that must stay free at volume
platform_matrix.notes: Free egress on R2, no cold starts, and Durable Objects give 30 seconds of CPU per request instead of 10 ms. This is the only platform in the list where a realtime voice agent is genuinely free to run.

platform_matrix.best_for: Next.js front ends and quick API routes
platform_matrix.notes: 120 second proxied request timeout and 100 deployments per day. WebSocket support needs a dedicated server, which the Hobby plan does not include.

platform_matrix.best_for: Public model demos with a Gradio or Docker UI
platform_matrix.notes: The fastest way to publish a model demo. Spaces sleep when idle, so the first request after a pause is slow.

platform_matrix.best_for: Long-running containers that need real sockets
platform_matrix.notes: Real WebSocket support without Durable Objects, but the free instance spins down after inactivity and the card requirement rules it out for a strictly free setup.

platform_matrix.best_for: Container workloads placed close to users
platform_matrix.notes: Legitimate free allowances exist, but the account must have a card on file.
